etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle French excentrique, from Medieval Latin eccentricus, from Ancient Greek ἔκκεντρος (ékkentros, “not having the earth as the center of an orbit”), from ἐκ (ek, “out”) + κέντρον (kéntron, “point”). Equivalent to ex- +‎ -centric.
senses: Not at or in the centre; away from the centre.
One who does not behave like others.
(slang) A kook; a person of bizarre habits or beliefs.
